Definition: from G4862 and G649; to despatch (on an errand) in company with:--send with.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says he desired Titus, and with him he sent a brother. Sending is done in company: Titus does not travel alone, and the brother sent with him is part of the message, because the gospel goes on two feet, not one.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's work is carried by companions, and I hold that sending in pairs is His pattern, not an accident.
